We need to decide for each column whether its value would already exist and be final at prediction time, given that prediction is made from the 1990 census and 1990 LEMAS survey, before the 1995 crime figures are published. The target is violentPerPop (violent crimes per population). So any column that is derived from crime data after 1990 (i.e., from 1995 crime figures) would be unavailable. Columns that are from census 1990 or LEMAS 1990 (law enforcement management and administrative statistics) are available. Also any column that is a demographic or socioeconomic variable from census 1990 is available. Columns that are crime counts (e.g., assaults, rapes, murders, robberies, etc.) likely are from crime data; if they are from 1995 crime figures, they'd be unavailable. However some crime variables could be from 1990 as well? The dataset likely includes crime variables from 1995? The description: "Prediction is made: from the 1990 census and 1990 LEMAS survey, before the 1995 crime figures are published". So we have only 1990 census and 1990 LEMAS data available for prediction. The target violentPerPop is presumably from 1995 crime figures (since we are predicting violent crime per population using 1990 data). So any column that is a crime statistic (like assaults, rapes, murders, robberies, larcenies, burglaries, autoTheft, arsons, etc.) likely are from 1995 crime figures (or maybe also from 1990?). But given the context, they are probably from 1995 crime data, thus unavailable at prediction time. However some columns like police-related variables (numPolice, policBudgetPerPop, policePerPop, etc.) are from LEMAS 1990, thus available. Also columns like pctPolicPatrol, pctPolicMinority, etc. are from LEMAS.

We need to examine each column name and decide.
